name: Shorshe Ilish
instructions: 1. Soak both types of mustard seeds with 1 green chili for 15 minutes, then grind into a smooth paste and strain if desired.
2. Marinate the Hilsa steaks with a pinch of turmeric and salt.
3. Heat mustard oil in a pan until smoking, then temper with nigella seeds and slit green chilies.
4. Whisk the mustard paste with turmeric and a little water, then pour into the pan.
5. Gently slide in the fish steaks and add enough warm water to partially submerge them.
6. Cover and cook on low heat for 5-7 minutes until the fish is tender.
7. Finish with a drizzle of raw mustard oil before serving with steamed white rice.
description: Shorshe Ilish is the crown jewel of Bengali cuisine. It features the prized Hilsa fish, considered the 'King of Fish' in Bengal, cooked in a sharp mustard sauce that perfectly complements the rich, oily texture of the fish. It is synonymous with monsoon celebrations and traditional Bengali hospitality.
